note: Phase 4b: Esme Vale's readings (Phase 4 Spec, The fortune teller). One line per card; the Sky is chosen by the weather two days ahead.

rows.text: Esme shuffles three times, taps the deck twice, and lays out three cards.
"Nothing much left to tell you, ranger. Sit anyway. No charge."
The Sky. Two days from now: blue all day. Wear a hat.
The Sky. Two days from now: grey, and in no hurry about it.
The Sky. Two days from now: rain. The kind that finds the gap in your collar.
The Sky. Two days from now: a storm. Stay where the roof is.
The Sky. Two days from now: fog. The trees will keep their secrets.
The Sky. Two days from now: snow. Quiet, and lots of it.
The Sky. Two days from now: wind. Hold on to your map.
The Sky. Two days from now: {weather}. The sky told me plainly.
The Path. Something waits that you haven't found. I've drawn where to look, roughly. Roughly, ranger.
The Path. Something small and old, off the trail. Look inside the circle, and look down.
The Path. Something wants doing that you've only half noticed. It's in the circle.
The Path. Blank, for once. You've found everything that's ready to be found. Well done.
The Heart. A gift for {name}: {item}. Their eyes would light up. Don't say I told you.
The Heart. {name} has a birthday coming: {when}. Cake is traditional. So are gifts.
The Heart. Tomorrow at {time}, {name} will be at {place}. Or so the card says, and it's never wrong.
The Heart. It shows you, smiling. You'll meet more people soon.
That's 10g, ranger. Pay on your way out.
"One reading a day, ranger. The cards get tired."
The caravan's curtains are drawn. Esme reads from six till late.
"A reading? 10g. Three cards: the sky, the path, the heart."
